title: Resolving roofs detect augmentation compatibility with unbounded targets
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], with integer-indexed cochain complexes, homotopy categories and derived localizations $Q_A,Q_B$ in a common larger universe [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal P$ contain zero, be closed under isomorphisms and finite biproducts, and have every object of $\mathcal A$ as an epimorphic image of an object of $\mathcal P$. Let $\mathcal R\subset K(\mathcal A)$ be the full subcategory of bounded above complexes whose terms are in $\mathcal P$, and let $D^-(\mathcal A)\subset D(\mathcal A)$ be the full subcategory of objects with cohomology vanishing above some integer. Let $E,G\in\mathcal R$, let $Y$ be any complex, and let $b:E\to Y$, $c:G\to Y$ be chain maps. Suppose $a:Q_AE\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_AG$ is a derived isomorphism with
$$Q_A(c)a=Q_A(b)\quad\text{in }D(\mathcal A).$$
There exist $L\in\mathcal R$ and quasi-isomorphisms $p:L\to E$, $q:L\to G$ such that
$$a=Q_A(q)Q_A(p)^{-1},\qquad cq\simeq bp,$$
where $\simeq$ means chain-homotopy: there are maps $h^j:L^j\to Y^{j-1}$ with $(cq-bp)^j=d_Y^{j-1}h^j+h^{j+1}d_L^j$ for every $j$.
Moreover, let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive and preserve quasi-isomorphisms between objects of $\mathcal R$. Suppose $S:D^-(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ is any functor equipped with isomorphisms $\rho_M:S(Q_A M)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_B(F(M))$ for all $M\in\mathcal R$, satisfying $\rho_N S(Q_A(f))=Q_B(F(f))\rho_M$ for every chain map $f:M\to N$ in $\mathcal R$. Then the derived isomorphism
$$\Theta=\rho_G S(a)\rho_E^{-1}:Q_B(F(E))\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_B(F(G))$$
satisfies
$$\Theta Q_B(F(p))=Q_B(F(q)),\qquad Q_B(F(c))\Theta=Q_B(F(b)).$$
In particular these identities hold for any such $S$ and $\rho$; $Y$ need not have bounded above cohomology, and preservation by $F$ is required only for quasi-isomorphisms between bounded above $\mathcal P$-complexes.

proof.text: Apply the right calculus of quasi-isomorphisms in $K(\mathcal A)$ and right-fraction representation to $a$. Choose a complex $T$ and chain representatives $s:T\to E$, $t:T\to G$, with $s$ a quasi-isomorphism and $a=Q_A(t)Q_A(s)^{-1}$. Thus $Q_A(t)=aQ_A(s)$ is invertible. Since each cohomology functor factors through $Q_A$, every $H^j(t)$ is invertible, so $t$ is also a quasi-isomorphism. Choose an upper term bound $N$ for $E$; then $H^j(T)\cong H^j(E)=0$ for $j>N$. No bound on $Y$ has been used.

Multiplying $Q_A(c)a=Q_A(b)$ on the right by $Q_A(s)$ gives $Q_A(ct)=Q_A(bs)$. Apply common refinement in the ambient category $K(\mathcal A)$ to the fractions $(1_T,ct)$ and $(1_T,bs)$ from $T$ to $Y$. It supplies $u_1,u_2:U\to T$ with $1_Tu_1=1_Tu_2$ a quasi-isomorphism and $(ct)u_1=(bs)u_2$ in $K(\mathcal A)$. Set $u=u_1=u_2$ and choose a chain representative. Equality in the homotopy category gives maps $k^j:U^j\to Y^{j-1}$ such that $(ctu-bsu)^j=d_Y^{j-1}k^j+k^{j+1}d_U^j$. The fraction theorem applies to arbitrary objects of $K(\mathcal A)$, so it applies to this $Y$.

source.place: Tag 04VJ, categories-lemma-equality-morphisms-right-localization, with common denominator the identity.

proof.text: Since $u$ is a quasi-isomorphism, $H^j(U)\cong H^j(T)=0$ for $j>N$. Use exactly the resolution clause of [lem-trf-resolving-class-derived-descent]: it gives a quasi-isomorphism $r:L\to U$ with $L^j\in\mathcal P$ and $L^j=0$ for $j>N$. Thus $L\in\mathcal R$. Set $p=sur$ and $q=tur$. On cohomology these are composites of isomorphisms, so both are quasi-isomorphisms. Cancelling $Q_A(ur)$ gives $Q_A(q)Q_A(p)^{-1}=Q_A(t)Q_A(s)^{-1}=a$. Put $h^j=k^jr^j$. Since $d_U^jr^j=r^{j+1}d_L^j$, precomposition of the preceding homotopy equation gives $(cq-bp)^j=d_Y^{j-1}h^j+h^{j+1}d_L^j$, as required.

proof.text: Write $P=Q_B(F(p))$ and $R=Q_B(F(q))$. Both are invertible by the preservation hypothesis, since $L,E,G\in\mathcal R$. All arrows in $aQ_A(p)=Q_A(q)$ lie in the full subcategory $D^-(\mathcal A)$. The assumed naturality for $p$ and $q$ reads $\rho_ES(Q_A(p))=P\rho_L$ and $\rho_GS(Q_A(q))=R\rho_L$. Therefore $\Theta P=\rho_GS(a)\rho_E^{-1}P=\rho_GS(a)S(Q_A(p))\rho_L^{-1}=\rho_GS(Q_A(q))\rho_L^{-1}=R$. This proves the first compatibility for the specified, arbitrary $S$ and $\rho$.

source.place: Tag 0794, proposition-left-derived-exists, common-roof comparison; elementary functoriality and the naturality hypotheses.

proof.text: Apply $F$ to the homotopy components: additivity and preservation of composition give $(F(c)F(q)-F(b)F(p))^j=d_{F(Y)}^{j-1}F(h^j)+F(h^{j+1})d_{F(L)}^j$. Thus these composites are homotopic and have equal images under $Q_B$. Consequently $Q_B(F(c))R=Q_B(F(b))P$. Substituting $R=\Theta P$ and cancelling the invertible $P$ gives $Q_B(F(c))\Theta=Q_B(F(b))$. Only $p,q$ were required to remain quasi-isomorphisms under $F$; neither $F(u)$ nor $F(r)$ was inverted. This proves the last assertion without exactness of $F$ or any cohomological bound on $Y$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_resolving_roof_ambient_compatibility {A : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} A] [Abelian A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A] {B : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} B] [Abelian B] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} B] (P : ObjectProperty A) [P.ContainsZero] [P.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms] (h_sum : ∀ (U V : A), P U → P V → P (U ⊞ V)) (h_epi : ∀ X : A, ∃ (T : A) (_ : P T) (e : T ⟶ X), Epi e) (E G : CochainComplex.Minus A) (hE : ∀ j : ℤ, P (E.obj.X j)) (hG : ∀ j : ℤ, P (G.obj.X j)) (Y : CochainComplex A ℤ) (b : E.obj ⟶ Y) (c : G.obj ⟶ Y) (a : Q.obj E.obj ≅ Q.obj G.obj) (ha : a.hom ≫ Q.map c = Q.map b) : ∃ (L : CochainComplex.Minus A) (p : L.obj ⟶ E.obj) (q : L.obj ⟶ G.obj), (∀ j : ℤ, P (L.obj.X j)) ∧ QuasiIso p ∧ QuasiIso q ∧ Q.map p ≫ a.hom = Q.map q ∧ Nonempty (Homotopy (q ≫ c) (p ≫ b)) ∧ ∀ (F : A ⥤ B) [F.Additive], (∀ (M N : CochainComplex.Minus A), (∀ j : ℤ, P (M.obj.X j)) → (∀ j : ℤ, P (N.obj.X j)) → ∀ f : M.obj ⟶ N.obj, QuasiIso f → QuasiIso ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map f)) → ∀ (S : DerivedCategory.Minus A ⥤ DerivedCategory B) (ρ : ∀ (M : CochainComplex.Minus A) (_ : ∀ j : ℤ, P (M.obj.X j)), S.obj ((resolvingRoofQMinus A).obj M) ≅ Q.obj ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj M.obj)), (∀ (M N : CochainComplex.Minus A) (hM : ∀ j : ℤ, P (M.obj.X j)) (hN : ∀ j : ℤ, P (N.obj.X j)) (f : M.obj ⟶ N.obj), S.map ((resolvingRoofQMinus A).map (ObjectProperty.homMk f)) ≫ (ρ N hN).hom = (ρ M hM).hom ≫ Q.map ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map f)) → (Q.map ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map p) ≫ (ρ E hE).inv ≫ S.map (ObjectProperty.homMk (X := (resolvingRoofQMinus A).obj E) (Y := (resolvingRoofQMinus A).obj G) a.hom) ≫ (ρ G hG).hom = Q.map ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map q)) ∧ ((ρ E hE).inv ≫ S.map (ObjectProperty.homMk (X := (resolvingRoofQMinus A).obj E) (Y := (resolvingRoofQMinus A).obj G) a.hom) ≫ (ρ G hG).hom ≫ Q.map ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map c) = Q.map ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map b))
